title: Identification of a novel UMOD mutation (c.163G>A) in a Brazilian family with autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease

reviewer.method: Direct full source reading and visual inspection where recorded; item-by-item selected/alternate packet comparison. Mechanical extraction/inventory is not read credit.

audit.exposure_note: Required full HANDOFF.md read on 2026-10-24 exposed aggregate source-audit counts, HG002/HG001/phenotype-only top1/5/10 summaries, compact 556/653/665 versus 430/649/665 of 681, corrected deltas, and the historical public FGFR2 rank 1 at 0.9654. Conservatively per_case, not blinded. No case ranking/outcome files were consulted for this review; only assigned source contexts, identities, availability, held primary sources and the adjudication validator were used.

patient_identity.statement: Exact pedigree identifier, sex and age match Table S1 for III:11.

genotype.statement: S1 positive group and Figure 1 + sign identify III:11 as carrying the shared heterozygous c.163G>A/p.Gly55Ser UMOD allele.
limitations: Modern NM_003361.4/hg38 coordinate normalization not independently shown by source.

segregation.statement: Multigenerational dominant segregation is reported and III:11 is genotypically positive; Figure 1 also shows clinically affected mutation-negative III:6. Reported LOD=2.58 with recombination frequency 0.15.
limitations: Do not infer complete penetrance or every parent-of-origin event; phenotype variability and affected noncarrier retained.

phase.statement: One heterozygous UMOD variant is reported; two-variant phase not applicable.
limitations: No additional haplotype or molecular phase measurement.

causal_confidence.statement: Family-level ADTKD-UMOD attribution rests on segregation, conservation and clinical pattern with negative REN/MUC1 testing; predictors are mixed and no allele-specific functional assay is reported.
limitations: Case-series attribution only, not recertification of packet PATHOGENIC/SOLVED labels.
